After the Mg was completely melted, the melt was held at 720–730 ◦C for 5 min and poured into a copper mould with 105 mm in diameter and 310 mm height.

The extrusion process was performed at 350 ◦C with an extrusion ratio of 25 and an extrusion speed of 1 mm/s. After extrusion, the sample was immediately quenched in water, and a rod with a diameter of 8 mm was obtained.
The cumulative area reduction of the drawing process was approximately 99.8%.
Annealing was conducted at 220 ◦C for 30 min for the wire after the final drawing deformation to eliminate part of the work-hardening.
After extrusion, the ultimate tensile strength (~263 MPa) and elongation (~11%) were significantly enhanced
Overall, refined microstructures can be acquired by introducing ~99.8% area reduction cold drawing deformation for the Mg-2.46Zn-0.69Ca alloy.

evidence.quote: A spherical Guinier-Preston (GP) zone with a coherent interface with the Mg matrix can be observed in the HR-TEM image [40], as shown in Fig. 5 (e).
Fig. 1 shows the microscopic characteristics of the as-cast Mg-2.46Zn-0.69Ca alloy. It consists of coarse equiaxed grains with an average diameter of ~50.17 µm, as shown in Fig. 1 (a) and (c).

After extrusion, the microstructure of the alloy is composed of two distinct regions, including fine equiaxed DRX grains and elongated un-DRX grains. The grains were refined sharply (comparing Figs. 1 (c) and Fig. 2 (b)) with an average diameter of ~2.0 µm, as shown in Fig. 2 (b).

evidence.quote: As shown in Fig. 4 (a), the wire has a non-uniform grain distribution, with most of the larger deformed grains surrounded by fine recrystallized grains. From Fig. 4 (e), the grain size distribution range is 0.75–11.25 µm in this condition, and the average grain diameter is ~2.1 µm, which is slightly larger than that of the as-extruded sample.
